evidence: The first two sentences put the learner with an inspector in an apartment before a final inspection signature, then name the three visible tasks: mirror shape, upholstery sample, and wallpaper pattern. The purpose of speaking is clear on first reading.

Each intro gives one new word and a concrete reason for its exact phrase: known single mirror form uses The shape is round; one near sample uses This material is soft; one distant wallpaper pattern uses That pattern is striped.

All 17 interactions were read in RU and UK. Each one has one assessable word, phrase, gap, or pair-grid action. Listening prompts offer localized meanings, not competing English sentences; the audio targets are shape, pattern, material, The shape is square, and one dictation phrase per task.

The three word-first contacts are distinct and complete before phrase practice: shape at 4/7/10, material at 5/8/11, pattern at 6/9/12, using listen/repeat/build or repeat/build/listen without adjacent identical families.

Distractors diagnose a single usable distinction: close sound (shape/ship/shade; pattern/patent/patter; material/matter/mature), form versus material versus pattern, singular versus plural, and number plus distance. The response-specific feedback states that distinction in both locales.
The final Those patterns are striped is a new target, farther-wall plural transfer, and is not an exact prior practice target. S56 checkpoint content does not appear.

The exact curriculum operation is a transfer across a/the/this/that/these/those by knownness, number, and distance. S55 exercises known singular The shape, near singular This material, distant singular That pattern, near plural These patterns, and distant plural Those patterns.

Grammar is accurate in context: a demonstrative replaces the article slot; The marks the named mirror form; plural forms use patterns/materials with are; distance contrasts are explicitly supplied by the prompt where That/Those is assessed.

The support curve is observable: isolated word contacts (4–12), a four-pair property grid (13), guided phrase dictation/gap/build/listen (14–17), then independent plural dictation, gap, and final build (18–20).
Every word card has a quoted native gloss and a short definition. All six active families are used with their prescribed input modes; no same family is adjacent and no target-family pair repeats.

No interaction asks the learner to process multiple English phrases. The Speed Match board is a permitted four-word pairing board, while each assessed phrase/audio interaction contains exactly one English phrase.
